newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Chechnya says talks with Moscow at dead end - Tass.
newsitem.headline: Chechnya says talks with Moscow at dead end - Tass.

text.p: Chechen President Aslan Maskhadov said on Wednesday talks on a lasting peace settlement between the breakaway region and the Russian government were at a "dead end", Itar-Tass news agency said.

"Negotiations on the conclusion of an agreement on the delimitation of authority between Russia and Chechnya have reached a dead end," Maskhadov was quoted as telling journalists in the Chechen capital Grozny.

He said Moscow, which withdrew its troops from the region last year after a 20-month military campaign against Chechnya's independence drive, had proposed four unacceptable new versions of a settlement in March alone.
Chechnya faced a "political and economic blockade", Maskhadov said, calling on Russian President Boris Yeltsin to intervene personally to reach a peace deal.
Maskhadov, whose military successes forced the Kremlin to negotiate a ceasefire last August, was elected president of the mainly Moslem North Caucasus region in January.
He has been insisting on winning full sovereignty but Moscow refuses to countenance anything more than autonomy within the Russian Federation.
On Tuesday, Russian media reported that Maskhadov, who is also prime minister, had appointed Shamil Basayev, Russia's most wanted man, as his first deputy.
Basayev, 32 and runner-up in January's election, led a bloody hostage-taking raid on the Russian town of Budennovsk in 1995.
Tass quoted a spokesman for the Russian prosecutor-general saying an amnesty declared for those who fought in the Chechen war did not apply to Basayev, who is wanted for "terrorism".
